initial.reason: Monomer1 is 1,4-bis(glycidyloxy)benzene-like (two epoxide/oxirane rings present as C1OC1 and C3OC3) giving multiple epoxy reactive sites for crosslinking. Monomer2 is m-xylylenediamine-like (two primary amines, NC-containing benzylic amines) providing complementary nucleophiles to open epoxide rings. The aromatic spacer in both monomers increases rigidity and polarity to target a Tg near 100 °C; the di-functional epoxy/di-amine pair gives moderate crosslink density (expected Er ~50) while remaining synthetically accessible and chemically compatible for thermoset formation.

best.reason: Revised to increase crosslink density and network rigidity. Monomer1 is a rigid aromatic triglycidyl (1,3,5-tris(glycidyloxy)benzene-like) bearing three epoxide rings (epoxide motifs written as C2OC2, C3OC3, C4OC4) to supply multiple C1OC1-type reactive sites and raise modulus/Tg. Monomer2 is tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (TREN) containing multiple NC linkages (multiple N–C connections/amine nucleophiles) to provide high functionality for epoxy curing. Epoxy (monomer1) — amine (monomer2) chemistry is highly compatible; the increased multifunctionality and the rigid aromatic core should raise Er (crosslink density) and move Tg toward the 100 °C target while addressing the previously low Er.
